title: Set up a folded tabletop easel with its rear leg out at the hinge stop, then rest a canvas on its ledge
instruction: Unfold the easel so its rear leg is out at its stop, stand it on its three feet facing the robot, and rest the canvas on its ledge leaning back against the easel, then let go of both.
context: Small easels like this hold menus, photos, place cards and paintings on tables everywhere, and they come folded flat. This one is a light beech A-frame (under 0.5 lb): its rear leg hangs from a brass hinge behind the top crossbar and swings out only as far as the hinge's stop. Nothing else holds it open, so the leg has to be got out to its stop and kept there while the easel is set down on its three feet; set down folded, it falls flat, and the light frame tips at a touch. Then a 1.5 in deep canvas has to sit on the 0.75 in ledge and lean back flat on the legs without pushing the easel over. Unlike a tablet's attached back flap, pushed open while the tablet rests on the desk, here a free-swinging leg on a stand about as light as a phone is opened while the stand is off the table, set down open and then loaded.
setup: Millimetres from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the table top. 1) Easel: U.S. Art Supply USA E-003 10.5 in Small Wooden Tabletop Easel (beechwood; listing: open 7.5 in wide, 8.5 in deep, 10.5 in set-up height, 0.75 in canvas ledge, folds to 11 in, under 0.5 lb). It lies folded, face up (ledge up), on its rear leg, feet toward the robot: the front face's foot end on the centre line at (120, 30), the frame along +x. Estimates (ruler and kitchen scale check them in a minute): front legs 279 long, 18 x 13 section, centre lines 172 apart at the feet and 72 at the top; top crossbar 231-249 up the legs; ledge 20-32 up, 19 deep, 190 long, with a 5 mm lip; rear leg 236 from the hinge pin (on the crossbar's back) to its foot, 18 x 13; hinge stop at 47 degrees between frame and rear leg; frame 147 g, rear leg 43 g. Open, it stands about 260 tall and 214 deep. 2) Canvas: U.S. Art Supply 5 x 7 in Gallery Depth 1-1/2 in Profile Stretched Canvas (USA GSC05X07G), 178 x 127 x 38, blank; about 170 g and 19 mm stretcher bars (estimates). It stands on one long edge, blank face toward the robot, its front bottom edge's middle at (250, -210). Frictions (estimates): beech on the table 0.5, canvas 0.55. Start: both arms at their ready pose, grippers open.
scoring: Judged at the end from the top-camera video, a photo and a ruler. Before the trials, open the easel by hand to its stop and measure its full depth D once (front of the front feet to the back of the rear foot, along the table; about 214 mm). Score 0 if the easel is not standing on its three feet at the end (lying, on its face, a foot off the table or still held up). Otherwise the lowest of: rear leg 1.0 if the trial's depth is within 10 mm of D, 0.75 if 10 to 30 mm short, 0.5 if more; canvas 1.0 if it rests on the ledge (its bottom on the ledge or lip along its whole length) and leans back flat against the legs (its face within 10 degrees of the easel's), else 0.5; let go 1.0 if both grippers are at least 3 cm from the easel and the canvas and both have been still for 1 s, else 0.25.
reset_notes: About 1 minute. Fold the rear leg flat against the back of the frame and lay the easel face up on its rear leg at its start place, feet toward the robot (mark the table at its foot end and side with low-tack tape once). Stand the canvas on its long edge at its place, blank face toward the robot. Wipe nothing: there are no liquids. If the easel or the canvas fell off the table, check the hinge still opens to its stop and the canvas corners are square before the next trial. Return both arms to the ready pose.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. The easel is two bodies on one hinge: a hard stop at 47 degrees (estimate from the published 8.5 in depth) and 0.004 N m of hinge friction (estimate); the brass hinge's own shape is not modelled. Bar sections, the crossbar, ledge, lip and pin positions, the rear leg's length, both masses (147 + 43 g; published under 0.5 lb), the canvas's bars and mass (170 g) and all frictions are estimates. The canvas is a 2 mm face plate on a hollow frame.
